chain.label: Runway 4L contaminated with packed snow and ice
chain.trigger: patches of one inch-deep compacted snow and ice. Runway sanded

chain.label: Crosswind with gusts during the takeoff attempt
chain.trigger: wind three three zero at one one...Gusts of up to 22 knots were reported in the general area near the time of the accident

chain.label: Inadequate B-747 slippery-runway procedures and simulator fidelity
chain.trigger: inadequate B-747 slippery runway operating procedures developed by Tower Air...and the inadequate fidelity of B-747 flight training simulators for slippery runway operations contributed to the cause of this accident

chain.label: Inadequate galley secondary cart-latch design/installation
chain.trigger: the Safety Board concludes that the material or installation of secondary latches in the galleys of N605FF was inadequate

chain.label: Captain overcontrolled nosewheel steering via the tiller at low speed
chain.trigger: the captain's failure to correct the airplane's deviation from the centerline resulted from his overcontrolling the nosewheel steering through the tiller

caused_by.evidence: overcontrol of the tiller on any aircraft would be more likely on a slippery runway than a dry runway

the B-747 has a tendency to react to crosswinds at very slow airspeeds with an initial, slight downwind drift. It would have been natural for the captain to have reacted to this slight deviation with a tiller input
As a result of the Tower Air procedure to guard the tiller during takeoff until 80 knots, the captain was ready to use the tiller during the beginning of the takeoff roll

chain.label: Nosewheel exceeded critical steering angle and skidded, causing an uncorrectable leftward veer
chain.trigger: the nosewheel quickly exceeded the critical angle at which the traction available for steering was maximized...the nosewheel began to skid...the airplane veered to the left

caused_by.evidence: when the pilots reacted to the decreased control responsiveness by adding more tiller, the nosewheel quickly exceeded the critical angle...Further tiller inputs in either direction were ineffective

chain.label: Captain failed to reject the takeoff in a timely manner
chain.trigger: the captain's failure to reject the takeoff in a timely manner when excessive nosewheel steering tiller inputs resulted in a loss of directional control on a slippery runway

caused_by.evidence: instead of rejecting the takeoff immediately after experiencing difficulty obtaining directional control, the captain continued to attempt to regain directional control with progressively greater rudder and nosewheel steering inputs

chain.label: Captain reapplied forward thrust during the rejected takeoff
chain.trigger: the captain abandoned his attempt to reject the takeoff, at least temporarily, by restoring forward thrust before the airplane departed the left side of the runway

caused_by.evidence: the Safety Board's CVR spectrum analysis clearly indicated that the thrust was partially reduced and then reapplied in significant amounts as the airplane left the runway

chain.label: Airplane departed the left side of runway 4L and struck ground obstacles
chain.trigger: the airplane then departed the left side of the runway...came to rest approximately 4,800 feet from the runway threshold and 600 feet to the left of the runway centerline

caused_by.evidence: The airplane then departed the left side of the runway

as a result of the reapplication of thrust, the airplane continued to accelerate as it approached the edge of the runway; this contributed to the severity of the runway excursion and damage to the airplane

chain.label: Serious injury to a flight attendant and minor injuries to passengers
chain.trigger: 24 passengers sustained minor injuries, and a flight attendant received serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: 24 passengers sustained minor injuries, and a flight attendant received serious injuries. The airplane sustained substantial damage
The two carts that came loose injured the R4 flight attendant and blocked the R4 exit
